experiment: 1H-13C methyl HMQC chemical shift perturbations from 20 conservative methyl mutants, mediation/Mapequation network analysis, at 750 or 900 MHz
buffer: 25 mM deuterated Hepes pH 7.2, 250 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 0.01% w/v NaN3 in 100% D2O
construct_or_mutation: His6 N-terminally tagged human p38γ; single-site mutants L77V, M81L, M109L, M112L, L116V, M120L, M137L, I150L, L159V, L167V, L174V, V186A, V187A, L198V, M216L, L225V, I238L, M239L, L268V, M291L vs wildtype
other_conditions: Protein 100–400 μM; 13C glucose labelling in M9; 73% of methyl resonances assigned; shifts in Hz at 750 MHz; related structures: homology model of inactive apo p38γ built with I-TASSER from p38α templates; no relaxation or exchange experiment performed
dynamics_type: ligand-/mutation-coupled long-range allosteric communication (time-averaged conformational ensemble redistribution); no timescale measured
author_claim: Mutation-induced methyl chemical shift perturbations propagate over >40 Å along the hydrophobic spines and define overlapping allosteric communities, with the R-spine partially preformed and dynamically connected in inactive apo p38γ.
anchor: In addition, we considered the full range of chemical shift perturbations down to very small differences, ~1 Hz, revealing subtle and underappreciated redistribution of sampled states in the conformational ensemble.
locator: Results, Identification of long-range perturbations; conditions: Methods, Minimally perturbing mutagenesis and NMR spectroscopy
caveat_note: Chemical shifts are time-averaged and report ensemble redistribution only indirectly. No exchange rate, population or relaxation was measured, so the paper gives no timescale or alternate-state structure. Mutations themselves may perturb the ensemble. The 'dynamic' R-spine statement is an interpretation of correlation networks, not a dynamics measurement.

experiment: 1H-13C methyl HMQC chemical shift perturbations from 13 methyl mutants in ATP complex, mediation/Mapequation network analysis, at 750 or 900 MHz
buffer: 25 mM deuterated Hepes pH 7.2, 250 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 0.01% w/v NaN3 in 100% D2O
ligand_or_partner: ATP and MgCl2 in molar excess (1:50) to inactive p38γ
construct_or_mutation: His6 N-terminally tagged human p38γ, unphosphorylated; 13 conservative methyl mutants vs wildtype
other_conditions: Mutants chosen quasi-randomly; 78 common methyl residues analysed across states; no relaxation or exchange experiment performed
author_claim: ATP binding completes the C-spine and reconfigures the allosteric network, creating two pathways between N and C lobes via the R-spine and via the αF-helix, docking site and C-spine.
anchor: Although the adenine ring of the bound ATP completes the p38γ C-spine, the unphosphorylated kinase is catalytically inert.
locator: Results, ATP binding to inactive p38γ reconfigures the network structure; conditions: Methods, Activation and ligand binding
caveat_note: Network analysis of chemical shift perturbations reports changes in coupling, not motion on a defined timescale. The mutant residues for this set are not listed explicitly, so residues are left empty. 719 pairwise correlations and 1066 three-residue paths were found; these are statistical outputs, not exchange parameters.

experiment: 1H-13C methyl HMQC chemical shift perturbations from 13 methyl mutants in dual-phosphorylated p38γ, mediation/Mapequation network analysis, at 750 or 900 MHz
buffer: 25 mM deuterated Hepes pH 7.2, 250 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 0.01% w/v NaN3 in 100% D2O
ligand_or_partner: apo, dual phosphorylated (Thr183/Tyr185) by constitutively active MKK6 (S207D, T211D)
construct_or_mutation: His6 N-terminally tagged human p38γ, dual phosphorylated; 13 conservative methyl mutants vs wildtype
other_conditions: MKK6 and ATP removed by Ni-NTA; dialysed against 25 mM Hepes pH 7.2, 250 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT, 1 mM EDTA; related structures: 1CM8 (activated p38γ) used as template for the activated homology model; no relaxation or exchange experiment performed
author_claim: Activation reduces overall flow but extends existing pathways, with the R-spine forming more extensive N–C lobe connections and the GHI subdomain joining the active-site community.
anchor: 625 significant pairwise correlations and 460 sets of 3-residue pathways were identified in active p38γ
locator: Results, Activation reinforces existing pathways; conditions: Methods, Activation and ligand binding
caveat_note: The evidence is network-level and based on chemical shift perturbations of static spectra; no dynamics timescale or population was measured. Residue lists for the 13 mutants are not given explicitly in the text, so residues are left empty.

experiment: 1H-13C methyl HMQC chemical shift perturbations from 12 methyl mutants in BIRB796 complex, mediation/Mapequation network analysis, at 750 or 900 MHz
buffer: 25 mM deuterated Hepes pH 7.2, 250 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 0.01% w/v NaN3 in 100% D2O
ligand_or_partner: BIRB796 (doramapimod), DFG-out inhibitor, in deuterated DMSO at 1:2 molar excess
construct_or_mutation: His6 N-terminally tagged human p38γ, inactive; 12 conservative methyl mutants vs wildtype
other_conditions: related structures: 1WBT (p38α DFG-out template used for the homology model); pH readjusted to 7.2 and insoluble BIRB796 removed by centrifugation; no relaxation or exchange experiment performed
dynamics_type: inhibitor-induced loss of allosteric coupling between lobes
author_claim: DFG-out inhibitor binding disrupts the R-spine and active-site communities, fragmenting the network and isolating the docking site.
anchor: The resulting community map reveals that the DFG-out inhibitor severely reduces connection and flow between the N and C-lobes
locator: Results, BIRB796 binding to inactive p38 causes network fragmentation; conditions: Methods, Activation and ligand binding
caveat_note: Network fragmentation is inferred from correlations (589 pairwise correlations, 500 three-residue paths) among shifts. It reports loss of coupling, not a measured motion or timescale. Part of the change could be a static structural effect of the DFG-out ligand rather than altered dynamics.
